title: Canon in D
description: Pachelbel's Baroque canon over an eight-note ground bass, now the most-played piece at weddings. Learn it to feel how a melody is built in layers over a bass that never changes.

arrangements.label: Beginner
arrangements.notes: The famous D-A-B-F#-G-D-G-A ground bass in quarter notes under the first four violin entries (two in quarters, two in eighths), closing with a short cadence; no sixteenth notes.
teachingPoints: Learn the left-hand ground alone first: D3-A2-B2-F#2 / G2-D2-G2-A2 repeats every two bars with the same fingering 1-3-2-5 / 4-5-4-3.
Right hand sits in a D5 position for bars 3-6 and drops to a D4 position for the eighth-note entries in bars 7-10.
Bar 10 has the octave leap D4 to D5: practice the last four eighths slowly with 1-5-5-4.
Count the eighth notes against the steady quarter-note bass before putting hands together.

arrangements.label: Intermediate
arrangements.notes: The first six violin entries over the ground bass, with the canon's second voice added in thirds in bars 5-6 and 15, and the two famous sixteenth-note entries (bars 11-14) kept intact.
teachingPoints: Bars 5-6 and 15 play the canon texture as right-hand thirds: keep both notes exactly together.
Isolate the sixteenth-note bars 11-14; the hand shifts at D4 (bar 11), D5 (bar 12 start) and B4 (bar 14) are marked.
Left hand stays on the eight-note ground throughout; play it from memory so your eyes can stay on the right hand.
Keep the pulse at 60 until the sixteenths are even, then raise the tempo gradually.
